holisticNarrative.summary:
This is one of the stronger publicly documented b10-style exports in this evidence corpus because it exposes a wide relational surface instead of a narrow standards-only projection. The table inventory is broad across encounters, medications, labs, messaging, referrals, insurance, and billing handoff, and the repeated GUID linkage pattern is a practical advantage for reconstruction.

The main weaknesses are not absence of data categories in the core EHR, but lack of import-grade semantic scaffolding: no formal FK map, no robust value-set publication for many status/code fields, and no sample payloads to confirm real-world nullability and edge cases. Those gaps move the posture from high-fidelity to usable-but-partial.

The highest boundary risk is around records that plausibly live outside core EHR capture (downstream payment lifecycle and some external portal or billing-service operations). If an implementation needs full financial lifecycle continuity, this export likely needs supplementation from adjacent systems.
standoutObservations: Surprising: encounter records include SOAP narrative fields directly, reducing note-loss risk compared with metadata-only exports.
Impressive: laboratory coverage is deep, with explicit order/result/specimen/observation/note/document slices.
Risky: no explicit PK/FK map or value-set catalog despite otherwise broad field documentation.
Unclear: DocumentStorageGuid references imply binary payload linkage, but public docs do not fully specify transfer packaging.

notableFacts: The v9 data dictionary contains 85 TSV entities and 1,165 documented fields.
The v9 index explicitly states manual export supports both single-patient and entire-practice population scope.
Encounter exports include narrative SOAP components (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) plus addendums.
Billing coverage is strong at superbill and insurance layers but does not clearly document full downstream payment/adjudication lifecycle tables.
No vendor-published machine-readable schema artifact (for example OpenAPI/XSD/JSON Schema) is present in the collected public docs.
Public documentation shows an active release cadence from v1 (2023-11-27) through v9 (2026-01-12).
